scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Rural Entrepreneurs to set up Custom Hiring Centres (CHC) of Farm Machinery
description:
The Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Rural Entrepreneurs to set up Custom Hiring Centres of Farm Machinery was launched by the Government of India on 1st April 2018. 

This scheme is part of the broader initiative to promote mechanization in agriculture and enhance the income of rural entrepreneurs. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to rural entrepreneurs for establishing Custom Hiring Centres. 

These centres are intended to facilitate access to modern agricultural machinery for small and marginal farmers who cannot afford to purchase such equipment. 

The scheme aims to promote the use of technology in agriculture, thereby increasing productivity and efficiency in farming practices. 

The government has set a target of establishing 10,000 Custom Hiring Centres across rural India by the end of 2024. 

Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided in the form of a subsidy linked to bank credit. 

The subsidy amount is up to 40% of the project cost for general category applicants and up to 50% for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs. 

The maximum project cost eligible for subsidy is Rs. 20 lakh. 

This means that a general category applicant can receive a subsidy of up to Rs. 8 lakh while SC/ST and women entrepreneurs can receive up to Rs. 10 lakh. 

The scheme also aims to create job opportunities in rural areas by promoting entrepreneurship among the youth. 

Eligibility criteria for applicants include being a resident of a rural area and having a minimum educational qualification of Class 10. 

Applicants must also be between the ages of 18 and 55 years. 

The scheme is open to individuals as well as self-help groups and cooperatives. 

To apply for the scheme, interested entrepreneurs must follow a specific application process. 

The first step is to approach a designated financial institution or bank that is empaneled under the scheme. 

Applicants must submit a detailed project report outlining the proposed Custom Hiring Centre's operations and financial projections. 

Required documents include proof of identity, proof of residence, educational certificates, and a bank loan application form. 

Once the application is submitted, the financial institution will assess the project report and determine the loan amount. 

If approved, the bank will disburse the loan amount, and the subsidy will be credited directly to the bank account of the applicant. 

The scheme also mandates that the Custom Hiring Centre must be operational within six months of receiving the loan. 

Disbursement of the subsidy is typically processed within 30 days after the loan is sanctioned. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, Government of India. 

The scheme is also supported by the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation of India (NAFED) and the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA). 

Contact details for further information can be obtained from the Ministry of Agriculture's official website. 

The scheme has been designed to ensure that rural entrepreneurs have access to the latest agricultural machinery, which can significantly reduce the cost of farming operations. 

The Custom Hiring Centres will provide services such as renting out tractors, harvesters, and other essential farm equipment. 

This will enable small farmers to utilize modern machinery without the burden of high purchase costs. 

The scheme is expected to enhance the overall productivity of the agricultural sector in rural areas. 

By promoting mechanization, the government aims to reduce the drudgery associated with traditional farming practices. 

Furthermore, the scheme is aligned with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The initiative is also expected to contribute to the overall economic development of rural areas by creating a sustainable model for agricultural services. 

Statistical data indicates that mechanization can increase agricultural productivity by up to 30%. 

This is particularly significant in a country where agriculture is a primary source of livelihood for approximately 58% of the population. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of skill development and training for rural entrepreneurs. 

Training programs are organized to equip applicants with the necessary skills to manage and operate the Custom Hiring Centres effectively. 

These training sessions cover aspects such as equipment maintenance, customer service, and financial management. 

The government has partnered with various agricultural universities and institutions to provide these training programs. 

The scheme also encourages the use of renewable energy sources in operating machinery, promoting sustainability in agriculture. 

The implementation of the scheme is monitored through regular assessments and feedback from beneficiaries. 

This ensures that the objectives of the scheme are being met and that the assistance provided is effective. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders in the agricultural sector. 

Many rural entrepreneurs have reported increased income and improved livelihoods as a result of establishing Custom Hiring Centres. 

The scheme has also contributed to reducing the dependency of small farmers on traditional farming methods. 

By providing access to modern machinery, the scheme has enabled farmers to adopt more efficient farming practices. 

The government continues to promote awareness about the scheme through various outreach programs and workshops. 

This is aimed at encouraging more rural entrepreneurs to take advantage of the financial assistance available. 

Overall, the Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Rural Entrepreneurs to set up Custom Hiring Centres of Farm Machinery is a significant initiative by the Government of India. 

It addresses critical challenges faced by small and marginal farmers in accessing modern agricultural technology. 

By facilitating the establishment of Custom Hiring Centres, the scheme aims to transform the agricultural landscape in rural India. 

The expected outcomes include increased productivity, enhanced income for farmers, and sustainable agricultural practices. 

As the scheme progresses, it is anticipated that it will play a crucial role in achieving the government's broader goals for the agricultural sector. 

The scheme reflects a commitment to empowering rural entrepreneurs and fostering economic growth in rural communities. 

The long-term vision is to create a robust network of Custom Hiring Centres that can support the diverse needs of farmers across the country. 

This initiative is a step towards building a more resilient and productive agricultural economy in India.
